generation.hypothesis: Applying high-pressure, high-temperature treatment to homogenized Al0.7CoCrFeNi will create a coherent hierarchical architecture that could approximately double both room-temperature tensile strength and ductility.
generation.material_initial_state: The starting material will be a homogenized eutectic high-entropy alloy with dual FCC/B2 lamellar colonies, incoherent interfaces, and strong-yet-brittle tensile behavior associated with interfacial cracking.
generation.intervention: The alloy will be treated in a hexahedron-anvil apparatus at 6 GPa and 1473 K for 2 hours, followed by cooling and decompression.
generation.conditions: Performance will be evaluated under room-temperature tensile loading after the specified HPHT cycle.
generation.structural_mediator: HPHT processing is expected to transform the dual-phase lamellae into a hierarchically patterned FCC/B2 microstructure containing coherent interfaces.
generation.mechanism: Coherent interfaces should promote dislocation transfer from softer FCC into harder B2, reducing pile-ups and local stress concentrations. Dislocations, stacking faults, microbands, and twins should jointly distribute strain more homogeneously.
generation.predicted_outcome: Fracture strength should approach 1.1-1.2 GPa and uniform tensile elongation 35-40%, approximately twice those of the untreated alloy. Failure should shift from catastrophic interfacial cracking toward distributed isolated microcracking.
generation.baseline: The comparator will be as-cast or homogenized eutectic alloy produced by conventional arc melting and casting, with limited room-temperature ductility and brittle interfacial failure.
generation.boundary: The synergy should depend on 6 GPa and 1473 K producing the hierarchical pattern; lower-pressure HIP or thermal-mechanical treatment at similar temperature would not be expected to reproduce it.
generation.uncertainty: The extent to which coherent interfaces remain stable through plastic instability is uncertain.

falsification_experiment.design: Compare untreated and HPHT-treated specimens by room-temperature tensile testing to approximately 35% strain and fracture.
measurements: Phase-resolved EBSD geometrically necessary dislocation density
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis will be rejected if elongated interfacial cracks persist or FCC and B2 GND densities fail to converge near 35% strain.

It also captures the change from catastrophic interfacial cracking to distributed microcracking, the lower-pressure processing boundary, and the key fracture-surface and phase-resolved GND tests.
